real: no markdown tags, keep it short: The extension's core feature is a "Manage Visitors" control and visitor-pass UI that it injects into Google Calendar event pages (https://calendar.google.com/*). This UI is delivered by a content script declared in the manifest, which Chrome only auto-injects into Calendar pages opened after the extension is installed or updated. scripting is used solely to call chrome.scripting.executeScript on Google Calendar tabs that are already open at install/update time, injecting that same bundled content script so the feature works immediately without the user having to manually reload their Calendar tab. Without it, an existing Calendar tab shows no extension functionality until refreshed. It is used only on the https://calendar.google.com/* host the extension is already granted, injects only the extension's own bundled content-script file (no remote or arbitrary code), and runs only in response to the extension's install/update event. It is not used to read page content or inject scripts into any other site.
prev_agent: Here's a justification you can paste into the **Privacy practices → `scripting`** field. It's written to match how reviewers expect the permission framed (what it does, the narrow trigger, the limited scope): --- **`scripting` justification:** The extension's core feature is a "Manage Visitors" control and visitor-pass UI that it injects into Google Calendar event pages (`https://calendar.google.com/*`). This UI is delivered by a content script declared in the manifest, which Chrome only auto-injects into Calendar pages opened *after* the extension is installed or updated. `scripting` is used solely to call `chrome.scripting.executeScript` on Google Calendar tabs that are **already open** at install/update time, injecting that same bundled content script so the feature works immediately without the user having to manually reload their Calendar tab. Without it, an existing Calendar tab shows no extension functionality until refreshed. It is used only on the `https://calendar.google.com/*` host the extension is already granted, injects only the extension's own bundled content-script file (no remote or arbitrary code), and runs only in response to the extension's install/update event. It is not used to read page content or inject scripts into any other site. --- A few notes: - This pairs with your existing **host permission** for `https://calendar.google.com/*`, which is what actually authorizes the injection — `scripting` is just the API to perform it. If the reviewer also asks to justify that host permission, the answer is the same: the visitor UI lives on Calendar event pages. - It's accurate as written — the only `executeScript` call in the code targets `content-scripts/calendar.js` into calendar tabs from the `onInstalled` handler, with no `world`/remote-code usage. - If they also flag **`notifications`** or **`alarms`** (newer fields on that tab), tell me and I'll draft those too (alarms = the 1-minute background sync poll; notifications = the out-of-tab "new visitor event" alert).
